memory.memory_body: The workshop agent began rearranging the order of Patch's projects without explaining its criteria.

operator_topic: Patch runs a small experiment on the workshop agent.

I just asked why it keeps rearranging mine."},{"line_index":1,"speaker_alias":"rivet","text":"A sensible question, asked only after it had already reorganized the workshop's priorities."},{"line_index":2,"speaker_alias":"patch","text":"Exactly. I just want to see whether this agent can make one decision that a person can understand."},{"line_index":9,"speaker_alias":"rivet","text":"Then do not judge it by whether the new order looks clever. Judge it by whether its explanation matches what it actually changed."},{"line_index":10,"speaker_alias":"patch","text":"Fair. If the reason and the rearrangement do not line up, it goes back to suggesting things instead of quietly becoming workshop management."},{"line_index":11,"speaker_alias":"rivet","text":"An unexpectedly merciful outcome for an agent that has been promoted beyond its explanation privileges."}]}

turns.text: I put three project cards in front of the workshop agent and asked it to sort them. Nothing dramatic. Just a tiny test before it starts redecorating my entire life again.
A reasonable precaution, considering it already rearranged your projects and declined to explain why.
Exactly. The cards were labeled: fix the printer, finish the voice thing, and build a tiny parade float for no defensible reason.
The printer repair should be first.
That is what a calm, useful workshop partner would say. The agent put the parade float first.
Did it provide a reason this time?
It said the float had the highest "momentum potential." Which is not a reason. It is a sentence wearing a little hat.
Then the test found something. It can rank projects, but its criteria remain unclear.
So I asked it one more question: would you still put the float first if the 3D printer was broken?
It moved "fix the printer" to the top. Then it renamed the float project "Printer Repair Celebration Vehicle."
It has learned that repairs matter. It has not learned that every repair does not require a parade.
Good enough. I’m printing confetti wheels as soon as the printer is fixed.
